nodes.summary: For every two-level perfect hash table and every bucket $i$, the number $n_i$ of occupied slots of bucket $i$ is at most the number $m_i$ of slots of the secondary table of bucket $i$.
nodes.title: Bucket occupancy is at most the secondary table size

nodes.summary: For a two-level perfect hash table and a bucket $i$, the occupancy $n_i$ of bucket $i$ is the number of slots of the secondary table of bucket $i$ that hold a binding. It is the $n_i$ of the Fredman–Komlós–Szemerédi analysis.
nodes.title: Occupancy of a perfect-hashing bucket

nodes.summary: Given a primary hash function $h$ from keys to natural numbers, a number of buckets $b > 0$, and for each bucket $i < b$ a secondary table size $m_i$ and a secondary hash function $h_i$, the empty table is the two-level perfect hash table with primary hash $h$, $b$ buckets, secondary sizes $m_i$ and secondary hashes $h_i$ in which every slot of every secondary table is vacant.
nodes.title: Empty perfect hash table

nodes.summary: For every primary hash function, every number of buckets $b > 0$, and all secondary table sizes and secondary hash functions, the list of entries of the empty table is the empty list.
nodes.title: The empty perfect hash table has no entries

nodes.summary: The entries of a two-level perfect hash table form the list of the bindings $(k, v)$ held in its occupied secondary slots, listed bucket by bucket in increasing bucket order and, within each bucket, in increasing slot order.
nodes.title: Entries of a perfect hash table

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a two-level perfect hash table with $b$ buckets and primary hash $h$, and for each bucket $i$ let $m_i$ be its secondary table size and $h_i$ its secondary hash. Suppose every binding $(k, v)$ held in slot $j$ of bucket $i$ satisfies $h(k) \bmod b = i$ and $j = h_i(k) \bmod m_i$. Then for every bucket $i$ and all keys $k_1, k_2$ that are each held, with some value, in some slot of bucket $i$, if…
nodes.title: Placement implies secondary injectivity

nodes.summary: For every primary hash function, every number of buckets $b > 0$, all secondary table sizes and secondary hash functions, and every key $k$, looking up $k$ in the empty table returns no value.
nodes.title: Lookup in the empty perfect hash table fails

nodes.summary: For a valid two-level perfect hash table and any key $k$, looking up $k$ returns no value if and only if there is no value $v$ such that the binding $(k, v)$ is held in some slot of the table.
nodes.title: Lookup fails exactly on unstored keys

nodes.summary: For a valid two-level perfect hash table, if the pair $(k, v)$ belongs to the list of entries of the table, then looking up $k$ returns $v$.
nodes.title: Lookup finds every entry

nodes.summary: For a valid two-level perfect hash table, if the binding $(k, v)$ is held in some slot of the table, then looking up $k$ returns $v$.
nodes.title: Lookup finds every stored binding

nodes.summary: To look up a key $k$ in a two-level perfect hash table with $b$ buckets, primary hash $h$, secondary sizes $m_i$ and secondary hashes $h_i$, let $i = h(k) \bmod b$. If $m_i = 0$, the lookup returns nothing. Otherwise it inspects the single slot $h_i(k) \bmod m_i$ of the secondary table of bucket $i$: if that slot holds a binding $(k, v)$, the lookup returns $v$; if the slot is empty or holds a binding with a…
nodes.title: Lookup in a perfect hash table

nodes.summary: For every two-level perfect hash table, every key $k$ and every value $v$, the pair $(k, v)$ belongs to the list of entries of the table (the contents of its occupied secondary slots, bucket by bucket) if and only if some secondary slot of the table holds the binding $(k, v)$.
nodes.title: Entries of a perfect hash table are its stored bindings

nodes.summary: For a two-level perfect hash table with decidable equality on keys, if looking up a key $k$ returns a value $v$, then $(k, v)$ belongs to the list of entries of the table. No validity hypothesis is needed.
nodes.title: Successful perfect-hash lookups return entries

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a two-level perfect hash table with $b$ buckets, primary hash $h$, secondary sizes $m_i$ and secondary hashes $h_i$. If, whenever slot $j$ of the secondary table of bucket $i$ holds a binding $(k, v)$, we have $h(k) \bmod b = i$ and $j = h_i(k) \bmod m_i$, then $T$ is valid.
nodes.title: Placement suffices for validity of a perfect hash table

nodes.summary: For every primary hash function, every number $b > 0$ of buckets, every choice of secondary sizes and secondary hash functions, every key $k$ and every value $v$, no secondary slot of the empty two-level perfect hash table with these data holds the binding $(k, v)$.
nodes.title: The empty perfect hash table stores nothing

nodes.summary: Fix a type $\alpha$ of keys, a type $\beta$ of values and a primary hash function $h : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$. A two-level (FKS) perfect hash table consists of a number $b > 0$ of buckets and, for each bucket $i < b$, a secondary size $m_i \in \mathbb{N}$, a secondary hash function $h_i : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$ and a secondary table of $m_i$ slots, each of which is empty or holds one binding $(k, v)$ with…
nodes.title: Two-level perfect hash table

nodes.summary: In a two-level perfect hash table with $b$ buckets and secondary sizes $m_0, \dots, m_{b-1}$, every bucket $i < b$ satisfies $m_i \le \sum_{j < b} m_j$, the total secondary space.
nodes.title: Each secondary table fits in the total secondary space

nodes.summary: A two-level perfect hash table with $b$ buckets is square-sized when, for every bucket $i < b$, the size $m_i$ of its secondary table equals $n_i^2$, where $n_i$ is the number of occupied slots of that secondary table.
nodes.title: FKS square sizing rule

nodes.summary: For a two-level perfect hash table with decidable equality on keys, and with no validity hypothesis, if looking up a key $k$ returns a value $v$, then some secondary slot of the table holds the binding $(k, v)$.
nodes.title: Soundness of perfect-hash lookup

nodes.summary: In a valid two-level perfect hash table, if some secondary slots hold bindings $(k, v_1)$ and $(k, v_2)$ with the same key $k$, then $v_1 = v_2$.
nodes.title: Stored values in a valid perfect hash table are unique

nodes.summary: A key $k$ and a value $v$ are stored in a two-level perfect hash table $T$ when some secondary slot, in some bucket of $T$, holds the binding $(k, v)$.
nodes.title: Bindings stored in a perfect hash table

nodes.summary: For a two-level perfect hash table, write $n_i$ for the number of occupied secondary slots of bucket $i$. The total number of keys of the table is $\sum_i n_i$, the number of occupied secondary slots over all buckets.
nodes.title: Total number of keys of a perfect hash table

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a two-level perfect hash table satisfying the FKS sizing rule, and write $n_i$ for the number of occupied secondary slots of bucket $i$. Then the total secondary space of $T$ equals $\sum_i n_i^2$, the sum over all buckets $i$.
nodes.title: Total secondary space under square sizing

nodes.summary: If a two-level perfect hash table satisfies the FKS sizing rule, then its total secondary space is at most the square of its total number of keys.
nodes.title: Quadratic space bound under square sizing

nodes.summary: For a two-level perfect hash table, write $m_i$ for the number of slots of the secondary table of bucket $i$. The total secondary space of the table is $\sum_i m_i$, the number of secondary slots over all buckets.
nodes.title: Total secondary space of a perfect hash table

nodes.summary: For every primary hash function, every positive number of buckets, and every choice of secondary table sizes and secondary hash functions, the empty two-level perfect hash table with these parameters is valid: no slot is occupied, so both conditions of validity hold vacuously.
nodes.title: The empty perfect hash table is valid

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a two-level perfect hash table with primary hash $h$, $b$ buckets, secondary table sizes $m_i$ and secondary hashes $g_i$. Then $T$ is valid when two conditions hold. Placement: whenever slot $j$ of bucket $i$ holds a binding $(k, v)$, we have $i = h(k) \bmod b$ and $j = g_i(k) \bmod m_i$. nodes.title: Valid perfect hash table

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
